data_section_full_text:
_4._ _Data Collection_


4.1 citation collection

We downloaded the SEC’s proposed and final releases from its website [(https://www.sec.gov/).](https://www.sec.gov/) We collected 176 proposed and 181 final
regulation releases regarding 191 unique regulation topics from 2007 to
2016 (2017) for proposed (final) releases (figure 1). <sup>10</sup> The 176 proposed
(181 final) releases cover 135 (140) unique regulation topics, of which 69
(46) releases have at least one academic paper citation in the document.
Proposed (final) releases have a total of 738 (389) citations. The remaining
107 (135) proposed (final) documents do not cite any paper. In sum, 879
unique papers are cited in proposed or final releases related to 191 different regulation topics. For 84 regulation topics, both proposed and final
releases are issued. These 109 proposed and 102 final documents are used
in the regression analysis, where we examine changes in citation patterns
for proposed and final releases. For an in-depth analysis of citations, we
use the information on individual academic papers cited in releases, such
as journal name, author name(s), publication year, and age of the paper.
When counting citations, we treat multiple mentions of one paper for the
same purpose in a single document as one citation. Citations of the same
paper in both a proposed and final rule within the same regulation topic
are counted as two separate citations.

We then combed through the citations and classified them as being
used to either highlight a potential benefit (discredit a cost), highlight a
potential cost (discredit a benefit), or neutral. <sup>11</sup> If one paper is discussed
for both the benefit and cost analysis within the same document, we count
them as two different citations—one for benefit and the other for cost.
We also tracked down all citations that were working papers when the SEC
discussed them, to determine whether, as of May/June 2019, the papers
had been published in a peer-reviewed journal and, if so, which journal. <sup>12</sup>


10 For proposed releases, we remove three amended documents and seven documents with
a title starting with “Extension of Comment Period for [rule name]” or “Re-opening of Comment Period for [rule name],” because they are not new or significantly revising regulation
proposals.

11 Examples of cost, benefit, and neutral papers are provided in appendix B.
12 We thank our research assistants for helping us categorize citation tones and hand-collect
working papers’ up-to-date publication information. Two research assistants read through all
